params.message:
Translate address words and keep old slugs of pages and frames alive

The word in front of a slug now follows the language: /en/collection,
/fr/collection, /de/kollektion and /en/frame, /fr/monture, /de/fassung
(blog categories: category, kategorie). Every word routes in every
language and answers with one 301 to the address of that language, so
the indexed /en/collectie/... and /en/montuur/... keep their value.

Pages and frames get a slug history like the blog's journal_slugs: the
sync remembers every slug a document had per language (document_slugs),
an old slug answers 301 to the current address, and the address of a
document that is no longer published answers 410. The table starts
filled from the mirror and from the slugs that were live on 2026-11-25.

Slugs are cleaned before use (App\Support\Slugs::normalize), and an
empty slug counts as missing: a language without its own slug borrows
the Dutch one. The English slug of the O1 was a sentence with spaces and
reached the sitemap that way; it now becomes a clean address, and the
spaced one forwards to it.

hreflang, canonical, the language switch, the sitemap and the collection
tiles use the new addresses. Checked: all 236 URLs of the live sitemap
answer 200 or one 301 to a 200 against a mirror of the published content.

Portal: Vertaalde adressen op hoet.be (/en/collection, /fr/monture, ...), en een gewijzigde slug van een pagina of montuur stuurt het oude adres door.
